name: Railway
summary: Railway runs web apps, APIs, and background workers as always-on containers, deployed automatically from your Git repo.

free_plan_covers.note: Ongoing Free plan gives only $1 of usage credit a month (after a one-time $5 trial credit), barely enough for light personal testing.

first_paid_usd_month.note: Hobby plan is $5/month and includes $5 of usage credit, covering up to 48 vCPU/48GB and a 5GB volume before extra usage bills.

portability.note: Railway runs standard containers built with Nixpacks or your own Dockerfile, portable to any other container host.

runtime_model.note: Services run as always-on containers, not request-triggered functions.

persistent_disk.note: Volumes are a native feature available even on the Free/Trial tier (0.5GB), scaling to 5GB on Hobby and more on Pro.

long_lived_connections.note: Services are regular always-on containers, so WebSocket connections are supported natively.

background_workers.note: Any service can run as a worker with no public port, staying always-on separately from a web service.

scheduled_jobs.note: A native Cron Schedule can be set per service; the shortest allowed interval is 5 minutes.

free_plan_commercial_use.note: Railway's pricing FAQ says commercial applications should upgrade to Pro; Free and Hobby are positioned for personal projects.

framework_support.note: Railway has official guides for deploying Next.js and SvelteKit (via adapter-node) as full Node servers; static Vite apps deploy the same way. It also has guides for Spring Boot, Django, FastAPI, Rails, Laravel, Express and ASP.NET Core, and runs a plain Go server from its Go support or a Dockerfile.

custom_domain_free.note: Railway's ongoing Free plan includes 0 custom domains, just the auto-generated up.railway.app subdomain, while the paid $5/month Hobby plan raises that to 2.

free_plan_sleeps.note: Railway does not pause services automatically; sleeping is an opt-in Serverless setting you turn on per service, which sleeps after 5 to 10 minutes idle and wakes on the next request with a brief cold start.

bandwidth_included.value: Free ($1/month credit): no bandwidth is bundled separately, egress is billed at $0.05 per GB straight out of that credit. Hobby ($5/month credit): the same $0.05 per GB rate with a bigger credit to draw from.
bandwidth_included.note: Railway does not carve out a free bandwidth amount; every GB sent out costs $0.05 and is deducted from your plan's monthly usage credit.

setup.step: Sign up at railway.com and start a New Project.
Choose Deploy from GitHub repo and select your repository.
Railway builds automatically with Nixpacks; add environment variables in the Variables tab.
Generate a public domain under Settings > Networking so the app is reachable on the web.

builder_notes: The ongoing Free plan only grants $1 of usage credit a month, which covers little beyond brief testing; budget for the $5/month Hobby plan for a real small app.
Railway's own docs recommend the Pro plan once the app is commercial; Hobby and Free are positioned for personal projects.
Cron-scheduled services must exit on their own when done and cannot run more often than every 5 minutes.
